title: SIU clears Toronto police officer in shooting death of man who stabbed him
subtitle: The officer was trying to arrest a man for dangerous driving when he was knifed in the arm and neck.
article: A Toronto police officer stabbed while trying to arrest a man for dangerous driving has been cleared in the man's death.
A Special Investigations Unit investigation concluded there are no reasonable grounds to charge Const. Jeff Blair in the shooting death of Peter Lumanglas, 38.
SIU director Ian Scott said Blair had authority to use lethal force against Lumanglas. "He had a reasonable belief that he was in imminent danger of dying," Scott said.
On April 15, Blair was conducting traffic enforcement using radar on Allen Rd. north of Lawrence Ave. W. He pursued a Dodge Caravan that was travelling at 146 km/h in an 80 km/h zone, the SIU said.

Blair lost sight of the van. Later, he saw a man, Lumanglas, walking quickly on a street. The report says the man was not dressed for the weather. Blair believed him to be the driver of the van. Blair spoke with the man, noting the man was sweating, seemed agitated and was nonresponsive when it came to questions about his driving. Blair arrested him for dangerous driving and failing to stop for police.
A pat-down search for weapons yielded a pocket knife and what Blair believed to be drugs. He told Lumanglas he was also being arrested for drug possession.
Lumanglas grabbed the pocket knife, which was on the trunk of the cruiser, and stabbed the officer twice in the arm and once in the neck, the SIU said. The report says Blair was bleeding profusely.
Blair then stepped back, pulled out his gun and asked him not to move. Instead, Lumanglas moved towards the officer with the knife raised above his head, according to the agency.
Blair discharged his firearm at least three times in the man's torso. The man fell and tried to get up again. Blair fired two more shots and Lumanglas fell back down, says the SIU.
Both men were taken to Sunnybrook hospital with life-threatening injuries. Lumanglas died of his wounds five days later. The officer underwent surgery and survived the knife wounds.
The SIU is a provincial agency that investigates cases involving police where there has been death, serious injury or allegations of sexual assault.
